faq.q: Do I need to supply the lights, or do you provide them?
faq.a: We supply all commercial-grade LED lights, custom wiring, timers, and heavy-duty clips as part of our all-inclusive rental and installation service. You don't have to worry about buying or replacing burnt-out strands.

faq.q: How much does Christmas light installation cost in Brantford?
faq.a: Most residential projects in Brantford range between $700 and $2,800 depending on total roofline linear footage, roof pitch, and whether you add tree wrapping or wreaths. Upload your photo for an exact line-item quote.

faq.q: When do you take the lights down in January?
faq.a: Takedowns begin January 2nd and run through January 20th, weather permitting. You do not need to be home for takedown.

faq.q: What happens if a bulb goes out or a storm knocks a line loose?
faq.a: Our 48-Hour Maintenance Guarantee covers all repairs. Simply text our team a picture of the loose strand, and an installer will stop by to fix it free of charge.

faq.q: Do I need a permit for holiday lighting on my Brantford home?
faq.a: A typical residential display on a single-family home doesn't normally need a municipal permit. If you're in a townhome or condo-managed community, check with your board first, and we can help coordinate that approval as part of your quote.

faq.q: Can you light the mature trees on older Brantford properties?
faq.a: Yes. Our bucket trucks and aerial lifts reach the larger mature trees common in areas like Brier Park and Myrtleville. We can wrap a trunk and lower canopy or light a single feature tree, and it can be added to any package during your free quote.

faq.q: Do you also install in Paris and St. George?
faq.a: Send us your address with your quote request and we'll confirm scheduling for Paris, St. George and other communities around Brantford.

areasHeading: What we usually light in your part of Brantford
areasIntro: Brantford is not one kind of house. Here is where we usually start for each area. Your photo tells us the rest.

areas.name: West Brant & Shellard Lane
areas.text: Newer two-storey homes with long roof runs and prominent garages. A clean C9 outline that includes the garage peak makes the biggest impression from the street.

areas.name: North End & Henderson Survey
areas.text: Larger homes on bigger lots near the 403, often with wraparound rooflines. Side runs and a lit front tree keep the display from stopping at the corners.

areas.name: Brier Park & Myrtleville
areas.text: Mature trees, larger lots and executive homes. The trees are the opportunity here: our aerial lifts reach the canopy a ladder cannot, so a wrapped feature tree can anchor the design.

areas.name: Holmedale & Brant Avenue
areas.text: Character homes near the Grand River with steep gables, dormers, brick trim and deep porches. A full C9 outline and a lit wreath at the entrance show off the architecture.

areas.name: Terrace Hill, East Ward & Eagle Place
areas.text: Older one-and-a-half and two-storey homes, often on tighter lots. We plan the runs around side yards and porch roofs, keeping the focus on the front elevation.

areas.name: Echo Place, Fairview & Cedarland
areas.text: Bungalows and family homes where a simple front roofline goes a long way. Add a lit shrub bed or a single front tree if you want more colour at ground level.
